pages.title: Landing Page
pages.description: Marketing homepage for OpenBat — positions the product as 'Google Analytics for AI chatbots.' Features hero section, problem/solution narrative, feature walkthroughs (ingest & analyze, prompt suggestions, stakeholder notifications, analytics), SDK integration code samples, FAQ, and CTA sections.
elements: logo carousel: Works with (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, etc.)

flows.name: Sign up from landing page
flows.description: New visitor reads the landing page value prop and clicks the CTA to create an account, beginning their journey toward setting up chatbot analytics.
flows.persona: Product manager at a company running an AI chatbot who wants visibility into conversation quality and customer sentiment.
preconditions: Visitor does not have an existing OpenBat account
steps: Land on the homepage at openbat.dev
Read hero section and scroll through feature sections
Click 'Start listening' button (appears in hero, mid-page, and bottom)
flows.expectedOutcome: User lands on the sign-up page and can create an account.
failureModes: If already logged in, CTA may redirect to /platform instead

pages.audience: Prospective customers — product managers, engineering leads, and CS managers evaluating chatbot analytics tools.
preconditions: None — public page accessible to anyone
pages.pageContext: Entry point for organic and paid traffic. Links to use cases, compare pages, security, contact, sign-in, and sign-up. Footer contains full sitemap of marketing pages.
keyActions: Read value proposition and feature explanations
Click 'Start listening' CTA to sign up
Navigate to Use Cases or Compare pages for deeper evaluation
View SDK code examples (Vercel AI SDK, TypeScript, Python, REST API)
Click 'Sign in' to access existing account
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands what OpenBat does and either signs up or explores deeper marketing pages.

pages.title: Sign In
pages.description: Email/password authentication page for returning users. Minimal dark-themed form with OpenBat branding, email field, password field, forgot password link, and sign-up link.

flows.name: Email login
flows.description: Authenticate using email and password credentials to access the main dashboard. Primary authentication method for existing users.
flows.persona: Returning user who already has an account and wants to access their chatbot analytics dashboard.
preconditions: User is not already logged in
User knows their email and password
steps: Enter email address in the Email text field
Enter password in the Password text field
Wait for authentication to complete and redirect to /platform
flows.expectedOutcome: User is redirected to /platform showing their organization's chatbot list.
failureModes: Invalid credentials show an error
Unverified email may block login
Banned users redirected to /auth/login?error=banned

pages.audience: Returning users who already have an OpenBat account and want to access their dashboard.
preconditions: User has an existing OpenBat account
User is not already logged in
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the landing page 'Sign in' button, or by direct navigation. Redirects to /platform on successful login. Part of the auth flow alongside sign-up and forgot-password.
pages.expectedOutcome: User authenticates and is redirected to the platform dashboard.

pages.title: Create Account
pages.description: Registration page for new users. Collects work email, password, and password confirmation. Sends a verification email on submit. Includes terms and privacy policy links.

flows.name: Email sign up
flows.description: Create a new OpenBat account with email and password. A verification email is sent to confirm the address before the account becomes fully active.
flows.persona: New user who wants to set up chatbot analytics for the first time.
preconditions: User does not already have an account
User has access to their work email
steps: Click verification link to confirm account
flows.expectedOutcome: Account is created and verified. User can now log in and is redirected to /platform where an organization is auto-created.
failureModes: Duplicate email shows error
Password too short shows validation error
Passwords don't match shows error
Verification email may go to spam

pages.audience: New users who want to start using OpenBat for their chatbot analytics.
preconditions: User does not have an existing account
pages.pageContext: Reached from the landing page CTA or the login page 'Create an account' link. After submission, redirects to /auth/sign-up-success.
pages.expectedOutcome: Account is created, verification email is sent, user sees confirmation page.

pages.title: Forgot Password
pages.description: Password reset request page. User enters their email to receive a one-time reset link. Links back to sign-in.

flows.name: Password reset request
flows.description: Request a password reset email when the user has forgotten their credentials.
flows.persona: Existing user who cannot remember their password.
preconditions: User has an existing account with a verified email
steps: Navigate to /auth/forgot-password (or click 'Forgot?' from login page)
Enter the email address associated with the account
Check email for the reset link
Click the reset link to navigate to /auth/update-password
flows.expectedOutcome: User's password is updated and they can log in with the new password.
failureModes: Email not found may show generic success (security)
Reset link expires
Email goes to spam

pages.audience: Existing user who has forgotten their password.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the login page 'Forgot?' link. After submission, a reset email is sent.
pages.expectedOutcome: Password reset email is sent with a one-time link to /auth/update-password.

pages.title: Chatbot List (Dashboard)
pages.description: Organization-scoped dashboard showing all chatbots. Displays chatbot cards with name, plan badge (Pro/Demo), API key prefix, creator email, last activity, conversation and message counts. Tabs filter by status: Active, Pending, Archive, Demo. Supports card and list view toggles.

flows.name: Create new chatbot
flows.description: Start the process of adding a new chatbot to the organization for analytics tracking.
flows.persona: Team admin or owner who wants to set up analytics for a new chatbot.
preconditions: User has owner or admin role in the organization
steps: Click '+ New chatbot' button in the top right
Follow onboarding steps to integrate the SDK
flows.expectedOutcome: New chatbot is created with an API key, and user is guided through SDK setup on the onboarding page.
failureModes: Insufficient permissions for non-owner/admin roles
Name validation errors

flows.name: Explore demo chatbot
flows.description: Open a read-only demo chatbot to explore the full OpenBat dashboard without needing real data. Useful for evaluation and onboarding.
flows.persona: New user evaluating OpenBat, or existing user wanting to see what a fully populated dashboard looks like.
steps: Click the 'Demo' tab to see demo chatbots
Click on a demo chatbot card (E-Commerce or SaaS)
Browse the read-only dashboard with sample data
flows.expectedOutcome: User sees a fully populated dashboard with sample conversations, analyses, and reports — all read-only.
failureModes: Demo chatbot data may not be real-time

pages.audience: Authenticated team members who want to select a chatbot to analyze or create a new one.
preconditions: User belongs to at least one organization
pages.pageContext: Primary entry point after login. Organization is auto-created on first visit if the user has none. Sidebar provides org-level navigation: Chatbots, Members, Settings. User can switch organizations via the org switcher in the sidebar.
keyActions: View chatbot list with status tabs
Switch between card and list view
Click a chatbot card to open its dashboard
Click '+ New chatbot' to create a new chatbot
Navigate to Members or Settings via sidebar
Switch organization via sidebar org switcher
pages.expectedOutcome: User selects a chatbot and navigates to its detailed dashboard, or creates a new chatbot.

pages.title: Organization Members
pages.description: Team member management page showing a table of all organization members with email, role (Owner/Admin/Member), and join date. Supports inviting new members.

flows.name: Invite team member
flows.description: Send an email invitation to add a new team member to the organization.
flows.persona: Organization owner who wants to give a colleague access to chatbot analytics.
preconditions: User has owner or admin role
flows.expectedOutcome: Invitation email is sent. Invitee clicks the link to accept and join the organization.
failureModes: Email already belongs to an existing member
Invitation email goes to spam
Role permissions insufficient

pages.audience: Organization owners or admins managing team access.
preconditions: User has owner or admin role
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the organization-level sidebar. Sits alongside Chatbots and Settings in the org navigation.
pages.expectedOutcome: Team members are managed and new members can be invited to the organization.

pages.title: Organization Settings
pages.description: Organization-level settings with editable organization name and a danger zone for permanent organization deletion.
pages.audience: Organization owner managing the org configuration.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the organization-level sidebar. Top-level settings for the organization (not chatbot-specific).
pages.expectedOutcome: Organization settings are updated, or the organization is permanently deleted.

pages.title: Chatbot Overview Dashboard
pages.description: Primary chatbot analytics dashboard with an AI chat interface ('What can I help you discover?'), quick-access command hints (tag entity, scope by plan, user/assistant analysis, scope by prompt), and summary cards: At-Risk Orgs, Performance (Resolution %, Quality Issues, AI Literacy), Activity (conversation count), and Risks (churn risks, yes-man, hallucinations). Each metric is clickable with sparkline charts.

flows.name: Ask AI about chatbot data
flows.description: Use the built-in AI assistant to ask natural-language questions about conversation data, sentiment trends, user behavior, and more.
flows.persona: Product manager who wants quick answers like 'What are users complaining about this week?' without writing queries.
preconditions: User is on the chatbot dashboard
steps: Type a natural-language question (e.g., 'What's driving negative sentiment?')
Optionally use command hints: @ tag entity, $ scope by plan, # user analysis, ! assistant analysis, ^ scope by prompt
View the AI-generated response with charts and insights
flows.expectedOutcome: AI responds with relevant data, charts, and insights based on the chatbot's conversation data.
failureModes: No conversations captured yet returns empty results
Complex queries may need rephrasing

pages.audience: Product managers, CS leads, or engineering leads who want an at-a-glance view of chatbot health and want to ask questions about their data.
preconditions: Chatbot exists and has been onboarded
pages.pageContext: Accessed by clicking a chatbot card from /platform. The primary workspace after selecting a chatbot. Sidebar switches to chatbot-specific navigation: Dashboard, Reports, Workflows, Prompt, Users, Conversations, Query Types, Deep Search, Analysis Config, Chatbot Settings.
keyActions: Ask the AI chat any question about chatbot data
Check performance metrics (resolution, quality, AI literacy)
Click any metric to drill down
Access conversation history via History dropdown
pages.expectedOutcome: User gets a quick health check of their chatbot and can drill into any area of concern or ask AI-powered questions.

pages.title: Reports
pages.description: AI-native reports page where users can create chat-driven dashboards. Offers pre-built templates (Customer Pulse, Sentiment Distribution, Risk Flags Leaderboard, Topics & Intents Overview) and the ability to create blank reports. Reports are built by chatting with AI which generates OpenUI widgets.
elements: cards: template cards (Customer Pulse, Sentiment Distribution, etc.)

flows.name: Create report from template
flows.description: Start a new report from a pre-built template to quickly get a populated dashboard with relevant widgets.
flows.persona: CS manager who wants a weekly sentiment overview without building from scratch.
steps: Report is created with pre-configured widgets
Optionally customize by chatting with the copilot sidebar
flows.expectedOutcome: A new report is created with pre-populated widgets showing relevant chatbot analytics.
failureModes: Template may show empty widgets if chatbot has no data for that analysis type

pages.audience: Team leads who want reusable dashboards and periodic reports on chatbot performance.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the chatbot sidebar. Reports are distinct from the AI chat on the dashboard — they persist as reusable dashboards.
keyActions: Create a new report with '+ New report'
pages.expectedOutcome: User creates or opens a report that visualizes chatbot data through interactive widgets.

pages.title: Workflows
pages.description: Automation hub for creating alert workflows triggered by analysis conditions. Three tabs: Workflows (list), Runs (execution history with status filters: All/Pending/Triggered/Skipped/Success/Failed), and Templates (pre-built workflow templates categorized by Alerting/Escalation/Reporting/Moderation/General).

flows.name: Create workflow from template
flows.description: Set up an automated alert workflow using a pre-built template, such as notifying Slack when an organization becomes at-risk.
flows.persona: CS manager who wants Slack notifications when churn risk is detected.
steps: Browse templates by category (Alerting, Escalation, etc.)
Click a template to preview it
flows.expectedOutcome: Workflow is created and will trigger automatically when conditions are met during conversation analysis.
failureModes: No webhook destinations configured
Analysis conditions don't match any data

pages.audience: Team members who want to automate alerts and actions based on conversation analysis patterns.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the chatbot sidebar. Workflows connect analysis results to external actions (Slack, Discord, webhooks).
pages.expectedOutcome: User sets up automated workflows that fire when specific analysis conditions are met.

pages.title: System Prompt
pages.description: Comprehensive system prompt management page with three tabs: Prompt (versioned prompt editor with timeline, publish mode toggle, kill switch, rollback, diff view), Experiments (A/B testing prompt changes against analysis tags), and Suggested (AI-suggested prompt improvements, coming soon). Shows prompt maturity level progression: Manual → Half-automated → Fully automated.

flows.name: Create new prompt version
flows.description: Write or AI-generate a new system prompt version, preview it, and publish it live to affect future chatbot conversations.
flows.persona: Engineer who wants to fix a hallucination pattern identified in analysis by editing the system prompt.
steps: Click '+ New version' to open the prompt wizard
Edit the prompt text (or use AI to generate changes)
Review the diff against the current version
Save as draft or publish live
Monitor analysis results to see the impact
flows.expectedOutcome: New prompt version is published and the chatbot uses it for future conversations. Analysis will track the impact.
failureModes: Publishing errors
Kill switch may need to be used if new version causes issues

pages.audience: Engineering and product team members managing the chatbot's system prompt and running prompt experiments.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the chatbot sidebar. Central place for prompt versioning, experiments, and AI-suggested improvements. The prompt can be in different maturity layers (manual, half-automated, fully automated).
keyActions: Create a new version (manual or AI)
Roll back to a previous version
Switch between Full and Diff view
pages.expectedOutcome: User manages prompt versions, runs experiments, and improves chatbot behavior based on analysis data.

pages.title: Users
pages.description: External chatbot user directory with a sortable, filterable data table. Columns: User (ID), Organization, Health score, Persona, AI Literacy score, Conversations count, Last Activity. Supports text search, faceted filters, date range picker, view customization, and pagination.
pages.audience: CS and product team members who want to understand individual chatbot user behavior and health.
preconditions: Chatbot has captured conversations with user identifiers
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the chatbot sidebar under 'Clients'. Shows the end-users who interact with the chatbot (not team members).
keyActions: Click a user row to see their conversations
pages.expectedOutcome: User finds specific chatbot users and understands their engagement patterns and health scores.

pages.title: Conversations
pages.description: Conversation list page with a sortable, filterable data table. Columns: User, Messages count, Outcome (Resolved/Partially Resolved/Failed), Issues count, Sentiment, Flags count, Last Message timestamp. Supports text search, faceted filters, date range, column sorting, view customization, and pagination (604 rows, 31 pages).

flows.name: Review a specific conversation
flows.description: Find and open a conversation to read the full message thread, see analysis results, and understand what happened.
flows.persona: CS manager investigating a flagged interaction to understand why a customer expressed frustration.
steps: Optionally use search or filters to narrow results
Click a conversation row to open the detail page
Read the full message thread with user and assistant messages
Review analysis results in the right panel (flags, outcome, persona)
flows.expectedOutcome: User understands the full context of the conversation including analysis tags, flags, and outcomes.
failureModes: No conversations match the filter criteria

pages.audience: Any team member who wants to browse, filter, and drill into individual chatbot conversations.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the chatbot sidebar under 'Clients'. Primary way to find and review specific conversations.
keyActions: Click a row to open conversation detail
pages.expectedOutcome: User finds relevant conversations and drills into them for detailed analysis.

pages.title: Conversation Detail
pages.description: Full conversation transcript view with chat bubbles for user (pink) and assistant (green) messages. Shows translation indicators, analysis tags (e.g., 'data visibility query'), expandable reasoning and tool call sections. Right panel has three tabs: General (Analysis Overview with flags, outcomes), User (user-specific analysis), Assistant (assistant-specific analysis). Also shows Persona matching and a 'Sharpen this analysis' CTA for deeper integration.
pages.audience: Any team member reviewing a specific conversation's content and analysis results.
pages.pageContext: Accessed by clicking a row in the conversations list. Breadcrumb navigation back to Conversations list.
keyActions: Expand reasoning and tool call details
Click 'View in' to see original context
pages.expectedOutcome: User fully understands what happened in the conversation and what analysis was performed.

pages.title: Query Types
pages.description: Semantic query type clustering page that automatically groups user messages into canonical question categories. Table columns: Query type (name + description), Volume (period), All-time count, Top intent, Sentiment, Resolved %, Last seen. Supports search, date range, view customization, and sorting.
pages.audience: Product team members who want to understand what users are asking the chatbot most frequently.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the chatbot sidebar under 'Clients'. Shows AI-clustered question patterns rather than raw messages.
keyActions: Browse query types sorted by volume
Click a query type to drill into its conversations
pages.expectedOutcome: User understands the most common question patterns and their resolution rates.

pages.title: Deep Search
pages.description: Semantic search interface that finds conversations by meaning rather than keywords. Single search input with a 'Deep Search' button and date range filter.
pages.audience: Any team member who needs to find specific conversations using natural-language queries rather than exact keyword matches.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the chatbot sidebar under 'Clients'. Complements the keyword search in the conversations table.
keyActions: Click search results to open conversation details
pages.expectedOutcome: User finds relevant conversations based on meaning/intent rather than exact keywords.

pages.title: External Customer Organizations
pages.description: Directory of external customer organizations whose users interact with the chatbot. Populated automatically when the SDK sends organization metadata. Shows empty state when no organization data has been captured.
pages.audience: CS managers who want to monitor chatbot interaction health per customer organization.
preconditions: Chatbot has conversations with organization metadata
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the chatbot sidebar under 'Clients'. Currently disabled in sidebar when no org data exists. Shows faceted filters and date range when populated.
pages.expectedOutcome: User sees per-organization health scores and can identify at-risk accounts.

pages.title: Analysis Config
pages.description: Comprehensive analysis configuration page with 7 tabs: Integration (5-layer integration maturity from baseline to DB-backed prompt with code recipes), Metadata (managed and discovered custom fields from SDK), Translation (auto-translate toggle with primary language selection), User Analysis (sentiment scoring, AI literacy, flags with custom definitions), Assistant Analysis (outcome types, issue types with custom definitions), Calibration (training examples for sentiment/intent/flags/outcomes/issues/faithfulness), Personas (AI-generated user persona cards with auto-discovery).
elements: integration layer cards with code recipes

flows.name: Configure analysis definitions
flows.description: Customize what the AI analysis pipeline looks for — add custom flags, outcomes, or issues specific to your business domain.
flows.persona: Product lead who wants to add a custom flag for 'pricing_complaint' specific to their product.
preconditions: User has admin or owner role
steps: Click the 'User Analysis' or 'Assistant Analysis' tab
Click '+ Add custom' to define a new analysis type
Configure the name, description, color, and priority
Optionally add calibration examples in the Calibration tab
flows.expectedOutcome: New analysis definition is active and will be detected in future conversations.
failureModes: Changes require re-analysis to apply to existing conversations

pages.audience: Engineering and product leads configuring how the chatbot's conversations are analyzed.
preconditions: User has owner or admin role
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the bottom of the chatbot sidebar. The most configuration-heavy page in the app.
keyActions: View integration maturity level and follow setup recipes
Track or deny discovered metadata fields
Toggle auto-translation and set primary language
Configure sentiment scoring levels and priorities
Add custom flag and issue definitions
pages.expectedOutcome: Analysis pipeline is configured to match the chatbot's specific domain, language, and business needs.

pages.title: Chatbot Settings
pages.description: Chatbot-level settings with 7 tabs: General (name, ID, creation date, analysis toggles, re-analyze, delete), Billing (Pro plan at $39/mo with credit usage and top-up), Company Info (product name, URL, description, industry for hallucination detection context), API Keys (ingest key management with prefix, status, last used), Members (chatbot-level access), Webhooks (Discord/Slack/custom webhook destinations), Import/Export Data (JSON/CSV export with analysis results, CSV/JSON import).
elements: forms and buttons for each section

flows.name: Export conversation data
flows.description: Download all conversation data including messages and analysis results for external processing or backup.
flows.persona: Data analyst who needs chatbot conversation data for custom analysis in their own tools.
steps: Select format (JSON or CSV, not visible but implied)
flows.expectedOutcome: Complete conversation data file is downloaded with all messages and optionally analysis results.
failureModes: Large datasets may take time to generate
File size may be significant for high-volume chatbots

pages.audience: Team admin or owner managing chatbot configuration, API keys, billing, and integrations.
preconditions: User has owner or admin role
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the bottom of the chatbot sidebar. Contains all chatbot-level configuration that doesn't relate to analysis definitions.
pages.expectedOutcome: Chatbot is fully configured with API keys, billing, webhooks, and company context.

pages.title: Chatbot Onboarding
pages.description: SDK setup wizard for newly created chatbots. Guides users through copying the API key and integrating the OpenBat SDK. Redirects to the dashboard once onboarding is marked complete.
pages.audience: Developer who just created a new chatbot and needs to set up the SDK integration.
preconditions: Chatbot exists but has not been onboarded yet (settings.onboarded !== true)
pages.pageContext: Automatically shown after creating a new chatbot. Redirects to dashboard if already onboarded.
pages.expectedOutcome: SDK is integrated and the chatbot starts receiving and analyzing conversations.

pages.title: Use Cases Overview
pages.description: Marketing page showcasing how different teams use OpenBat. Links to dedicated pages for Customer Success, Engineering, Product Teams, and Support use cases.
pages.audience: Prospective customers evaluating OpenBat for their specific team's needs.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the top navigation 'Use cases' dropdown or footer links.
keyActions: Navigate to specific use case pages
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands how OpenBat applies to their team's specific needs.

pages.title: Use Case — Customer Success
pages.description: Marketing page focused on how CS teams use OpenBat to detect churn risk, surface at-risk accounts, and monitor sentiment before renewal reviews.
pages.audience: Customer success managers evaluating chatbot analytics tools.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from Use Cases overview or nav dropdown. One of 4 team-specific use case pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: CS manager understands the specific value OpenBat provides for churn risk and account health monitoring.

pages.title: Use Case — Engineering
pages.description: Marketing page focused on how engineering teams use OpenBat to catch hallucinations, monitor chatbot quality, and validate prompt changes.
pages.audience: Engineering leads evaluating chatbot quality monitoring tools.
pages.pageContext: One of 4 team-specific use case pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Engineer understands how OpenBat helps detect hallucinations and quality issues.

pages.title: Use Case — Product Teams
pages.description: Marketing page focused on how product teams use OpenBat to understand what users ask for, ranked by demand and sentiment.
pages.audience: Product managers evaluating tools for understanding chatbot user needs.
pages.pageContext: One of 4 team-specific use case pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: PM understands how OpenBat surfaces feature requests and user intent patterns.

pages.title: Use Case — Support
pages.description: Marketing page focused on how support teams use OpenBat to triage frustration and resolve issues faster.
pages.audience: Support team leads evaluating chatbot triage tools.
pages.pageContext: One of 4 team-specific use case pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Support lead understands how OpenBat helps prioritize frustrated users.

pages.title: Compare Overview
pages.description: Marketing page positioning OpenBat against LLM observability tools. Highlights that competitors count tokens while OpenBat surfaces business intelligence (churn, sentiment, feature requests).
pages.audience: Prospective customers comparing OpenBat to alternatives like Langfuse, LangSmith, Helicone, and Braintrust.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the top navigation 'Compare' dropdown or footer links. Links to 6 specific comparison pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands how OpenBat differs from the alternatives.

pages.title: Compare — vs Langfuse
pages.description: Head-to-head comparison page positioning OpenBat (business intelligence for product/CS teams) against Langfuse (LLM tracing for engineers).
pages.audience: Teams evaluating Langfuse who want to understand the difference.
pages.pageContext: One of 6 competitor comparison pages. Same template as other /compare/* pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands the key differences and decides which tool fits their needs.

pages.title: Compare — vs LangSmith
pages.description: Comparison page: OpenBat vs LangSmith (tracing tool vs business intelligence).
pages.audience: Teams evaluating LangSmith.
pages.pageContext: One of 6 competitor comparison pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands the positioning difference.

pages.title: Compare — vs Helicone
pages.description: Comparison page: OpenBat vs Helicone (API logs vs conversation insight).
pages.audience: Teams evaluating Helicone.
pages.pageContext: One of 6 competitor comparison pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands the positioning difference.

pages.title: Compare — vs Braintrust
pages.description: Comparison page: OpenBat vs Braintrust (eval suite vs ongoing monitoring).
pages.audience: Teams evaluating Braintrust.
pages.pageContext: One of 6 competitor comparison pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands the positioning difference.

pages.title: Compare — vs Manual Review
pages.description: Comparison page: OpenBat vs manual spreadsheet-based conversation review.
pages.audience: Teams currently reviewing conversations manually.
pages.pageContext: One of 6 competitor comparison pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands the efficiency gains of automated analysis.

pages.title: Compare — vs DIY
pages.description: Comparison page: OpenBat vs building your own analytics pipeline.
pages.audience: Engineering teams considering building in-house.
pages.pageContext: One of 6 competitor comparison pages.
pages.expectedOutcome: Visitor understands the time/cost tradeoff of building vs using OpenBat.

pages.title: Contact
pages.description: Demo booking and contact page. Features a live thread illustration showing conversation analysis in action (churn risk detection). Includes a contact form for booking a demo, with a 24-hour response guarantee.
pages.audience: Prospective customers who want a personalized demo of OpenBat.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the top navigation or footer. Terminal marketing page for high-intent visitors.
pages.expectedOutcome: Demo request is submitted and the team responds within 24 hours.

pages.title: Security
pages.description: Security information page detailing OpenBat's data protection practices. Covers encryption (TLS 1.2+, AES-256-GCM), data handling, access controls, compliance, sub-processors, incident response, and privacy. Links to downloadable documents: DPA, Sub-processors list, Privacy policy, Security FAQ.
elements: document links: DPA/Sub-processors/Privacy policy/Security FAQ/Contact security
pages.audience: Security-conscious prospects and compliance teams evaluating OpenBat.
pages.pageContext: Accessed from the top navigation or footer. Important for enterprise evaluation.
pages.expectedOutcome: Security team is satisfied with OpenBat's data protection practices.
